title: SecOps-NG DORA Article 19 Technical-Incident Report Variant
description: Typed shape for the technical-incident report an in-scope financial entity must produce under Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 (DORA) Article 19(4) and the Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2024/2956 ITS on the standard forms, templates and procedures for reporting major ICT-related incidents. One report record is produced per (incident_id, milestone) — one of the four entries on the DORA Article 19 reporting chain (initial_4h, intermediate_72h, final_1mo, voluntary_cyber_threat). The report variant is derived deterministically from the F-WF-05 incident_management workflow's timeline records (one TimelineSession per incident_id, three RegulatorSubmissionReceipts plus a TimelineClosure per major-incident lifecycle); the variant->timeline-record field derivations are documented in content/mappings/dora/article-19-report-variant.md. SKELETON layer: required-field shape and the high-level classification / timeline_refs / impact_indicators / mitigation_status envelopes are pinned so a CORE sibling card can bind a per-target compiler against a stable contract. Inner shapes are intentionally permissive at this layer and tightened in EXTEND once the per-target emitter work lands. Public-bar artifact: no individual personal names, no operator branding, no internal infrastructure references. Out of scope: the actual ITS submission transport (operator-owned per AGENTS.md §3) and per-Member-State CSIRT routing.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject reports produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship. SKELETON layer carries 0.1.0; the CORE sibling card lifts it to 1.0.0 once the per-target emitters land and the inner envelopes are tightened.

report_id.description: Stable per-report identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<incident_id>|<report_variant>|<submitted_at>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Two submissions of the same variant on the same incident at the same instant collide deliberately; a replay of the same submission stays byte-identical.

report_variant.description: Which DORA Article 19 reporting-chain milestone this report record fills. Imports the shared vocabulary from schemas/dora_art19_report_milestone.json. The four enum values map onto entries dora:art-19-initial-4h, dora:art-19-intermediate-72h, dora:art-19-final-one-month, dora:art-19-cyber-threat-voluntary in content/mappings/dora/article-19-and-28.yaml.

incident_id.description: Stable case identifier for the incident as a UUID (RFC 4122). Issued upstream by the F-WF-05 timeline-open primitive (content/playbooks/incident_management/primitives/timeline_binding.open_timeline) so every milestone report on the chain pins against one id and a replay-vs-original comparison is single-string-equal.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this report variant helps satisfy. At least one entry — a DORA Art. 19 report with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-SV-03 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/dora/article-19-and-28.yaml via the `id` field. Typical entries: dora:art-19-initial-4h, dora:art-19-intermediate-72h, dora:art-19-final-one-month, dora:art-19-cyber-threat-voluntary, optionally dora:art-18-classification.

classification.description: Deterministic outputs of the DORA Article 18(1) major-ICT-incident classifier (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772). At the SKELETON layer the inner shape mirrors the F-WF-05 ClassificationVerdict dataclass (significant + cross_border + reasons + rule_ids) plus a `major` flag that is the DORA-side equivalent of the NIS2 `significant` flag. TODO(CORE): replace the SKELETON parallel-flag arrangement with a single shared classification verdict once the F-WF-05 classifier exposes a DORA materiality-threshold rule pack.

major.description: DORA Article 18(1) major-classification flag (the criteria operationalised by Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1772). When false the operator should not be emitting an Art. 19 report at all; the schema enforces the field's presence so a downstream replay can audit-trail the decision.

cross_border.description: Optional cross-border-scope flag. Reserved for the EXTEND sibling card's tightening of the DORA cross-border materiality criteria; the SKELETON layer mirrors the NIS2 Article 23(6) shape so a CORE-FANOUT card can read the same field across both reporting chains.

recurring_incident.description: DORA Article 18(2) recurring-incident flag. True when the report is being filed under the six-month rolling aggregation rule. SKELETON layer reserves the field; the EXTEND sibling card pins the supporting `recurring_cluster_ref` once the recurring-incident correlator lands.

reasons.description: Ordered list of human-readable rule-reason strings from the classification verdict. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names.

rule_ids.description: Ordered list of policy rule ids from the classification verdict (e.g. `dora.sig.severe_disruption`, `dora.cb.multi_member_state`). SKELETON-layer permissive pattern; the EXTEND sibling card tightens this to a shared dora.<class>.<rule> alphabet once the DORA rule pack lands.

timeline_refs.description: Pointers into the F-WF-05 incident_management timeline that this report variant was derived from. Mirrors the (clock_started_at, submitted_at) shape used by the incidents evidence stream's notification_timeline[] entries so a downstream consumer can correlate a DORA Art. 19 report record against the same F-WF-05 TimelineSession by `timeline_handle`. SKELETON layer pins the three required pointers; EXTEND tightens the optional fields once the per-target emitters land.

timeline_handle.description: Opaque handle returned by the F-WF-05 open_timeline primitive (TimelineSession.handle). Carried verbatim so the regulator-side acknowledgement can be correlated back onto the timeline JSON artifact persisted at content/evidence/incidents/<incident_id>/timeline.json.

clock_started_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the regulator clock for this report variant started — typically the F-WF-05 TimelineSession.opened_at instant (i.e. the operator's classification-as-major instant for the 4h/72h variants, or the intermediate-submission instant for the 1mo variant).

stage_event_id.description: F-WF-05 TimelineEvent.event_id (a 16-hex-digit digest) of the regulator-submission timeline event the report record corresponds to. Lets a replay-vs-original comparison resolve to a single string-equal check.

previous_milestone_event_id.description: Optional F-WF-05 TimelineEvent.event_id of the prior milestone on the chain (e.g. the intermediate_72h event_id when this is the final_1mo report). SKELETON layer reserves the field; the CORE sibling card pins it required for intermediate_72h and final_1mo once the cross-milestone derivation is exercised end-to-end.

impact_indicators.description: Per-Art. 19(4) impact indicators an operator must populate at the relevant milestone. SKELETON layer carries a permissive envelope so an emitter can land a minimal initial_4h report (most fields TODO) and a richer final_1mo report (most fields populated). EXTEND-schema sibling card tightens the inner shapes — the Commission ITS (EU) 2024/2956 field-level vocabulary lands then.

affected_functions.description: Operator-supplied identifiers for the critical or important functions affected. Free-text at the SKELETON layer; EXTEND-schema tightens to the operator's function-catalogue references.

affected_clients_count.description: Operator-graded count of clients affected by the incident. Non-negative integer. `null` when not yet known at the milestone (typical for initial_4h).

duration_minutes.description: Operator-graded incident duration in minutes (closed at recovery). Non-negative. `null` when the incident is still open (typical for initial_4h and intermediate_72h).

geographic_scope.description: Member States and/or third countries affected. ISO-3166 alpha-2 country codes. Empty array allowed at SKELETON (TODO at initial_4h); EXTEND-schema tightens the minimum cardinality per milestone.

data_loss_indicator.description: Operator-graded indicator of whether the incident involved confidentiality, integrity, or availability impact on data. SKELETON-layer enum closely mirroring the NIS2 incidents stream's classification.severity but expressed as a CIA-triad band; the EXTEND-schema sibling card lifts this into a shared vocabulary at schemas/dora_data_impact.json.

indicators_of_compromise.description: Stable identifiers of the IoCs the operator has at this milestone. Mirrors the NotificationSubmission.indicators_of_compromise shape on the F-WF-05 regulator-submission contract so a single emitter populates both reports. Empty array is valid (typical for initial_4h).

mitigation_status.description: Per-milestone mitigation status. At initial_4h / intermediate_72h this names actions in flight; at final_1mo it names completed remediations and any residual-risk statement. SKELETON layer reserves a permissive shape; EXTEND-schema tightens the action-record vocabulary once the per-target emitters land.

state.description: Coarse mitigation-state band. SKELETON-layer enum; the EXTEND-schema sibling card lifts this into a shared vocabulary at schemas/dora_mitigation_state.json once the per-target emitters land.

actions_in_flight.description: Free-text summaries of mitigation actions currently in progress. Public-bar text: no individual names, no operator branding.

completed_actions.description: Free-text summaries of remediation actions completed by the milestone instant. Required content for final_1mo (Art. 19(4)(c)); typically empty for initial_4h.

root_cause.description: Operator-readable root-cause description for the final_1mo variant (Art. 19(4)(c)). `null` for initial_4h and intermediate_72h. SKELETON layer treats this as optional shape; EXTEND-schema pins it required when report_variant == final_1mo via an oneOf/$conditional refinement once the per-target emitters land. Public-bar text: no operator branding, no individual names. Carried by the F-WF-05 FinalReportSubmission.root_cause DSPy-mediated free-text field (content/playbooks/incident_management/primitives/regulator_submission.py).

residual_risk.description: Operator-readable residual-risk statement for the final_1mo variant (Art. 19(4)(c)). `null` for earlier milestones. SKELETON layer optional; EXTEND-schema pins it required when report_variant == final_1mo.

submitted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which the report was submitted to the competent authority (or the closest evidentiary equivalent). Stable input to the report_id derivation so re-emissions in the same submission at the same instant stay byte-identical.

submission_ref.description: Operator-side opaque reference for the submission (regulator portal receipt id, CSIRT ticket id, URN). Free-text constrained — no commentary, no operator branding. Optional at SKELETON layer (a replay-from-history record may not carry a regulator receipt).

provenance.description: Where this report came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/evidence/*/schemas/* so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to the source workflow run.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this report. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the report-level submitted_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.
